sources.note: RFC 7519 JWT core spec: unsecured (alg=none) JWT definition, the application-level rule that an acceptable-algorithm check is required even on successful validation, and the registered claim names iss/sub/aud/exp/nbf.
RFC 7636 PKCE: code_verifier/code_challenge mechanics, and the token-endpoint rule that the server recomputes the challenge from the received verifier and compares it to the recorded one.
RFC 6749 OAuth 2.0 framework: the rule that the authorization server must not automatically redirect to a URI it has not validated, and the exact-redirect-URI requirement.
OAuth grant-type definitions and the token endpoint request/response contract used for validating code redemption.
RFC 6750 bearer token usage: why tokens in URI query parameters leak, and the WWW-Authenticate challenge format.
RFC 9207 authorization server issuer identification: the iss response parameter used for mix-up defence.
RFC 9449 DPoP: sender-constrained access tokens, the proof-of-possession alternative to mTLS binding.
RFC 8705 mTLS client authentication and certificate-bound access tokens.
RFC 3986 URI generic syntax: the simple-string-comparison rule that exact redirect_uri matching depends on.
RFC 1918 private address ranges, useful for building an address-space test matrix against an SSRF filter.
RFC 7515 JWS: the alg/typ/kid/jku/x5u header parameter definitions and the crit extension.
RFC 7517 JWK: key material representation and the x5c/x5u fields relevant to header-supplied key material.
RFC 7518 JWA: algorithm identifiers including HS256/RS256 and the compression option relevant to algorithm-confusion testing.
Django deployment security checklist: cross-site scripting, clickjacking, host header validation and the settings that affect each.
QuerySet API reference: the filter/exclude/get surface where object-scoping bugs are introduced.
View layer reference: how per-request authorisation is typically wired in a Django application.
Staticfiles finders: how development-time asset discovery differs from a plain document-root serve.
Offset vs cursor pagination, including the explicit note that offset pagination has performance and security downsides for larger data sets.
The node global-identification pattern: a single lookup field that collapses many IDOR surfaces into one query.
GraphQL execution model basics: the schema, the type system and the single endpoint premise behind most GraphQL technique findings.
GraphQL specification: normative language for execution, error propagation, and the introspection schema.
Oracle text literals: alternative quoting mechanism (q'...') and the single-quote doubling rule.
SQLite transaction semantics: relevant to second-order SQLi where a write commits before the payload is reused.
FTS5 full-text query grammar: column filters, NEAR, quoted phrases and brace alternation in the MATCH operand.
Redirect-specific protocol allow-list; documents the permissive default and that CURLOPT_PROTOCOLS_STR denials are not overridden by it.
Go net/url package reference: Parse vs ParseRequestURI context differences that produce parser differentials.
Kernel network sysctls including rp_filter and route_localnet, which change whether a private-range address is reachable at all.
RFC 9110 status codes and method semantics, used to distinguish GraphQL's HTTP-layer framing from GraphQL's own error model.
CSP Level 2: nonce and hash source expressions, the basis for judging a nonce-based policy on a specific landing page.
DOM standard: postMessage origin handling, innerHTML setter behaviour and Node tree mutation rules.
WHATWG URL standard: the single URL parsing algorithm, used as the reference when a server-side parser disagrees with the browser's.
ECMAScript specification: string, template-literal and eval semantics for reasoning about JS-string injection contexts.
Active Record query interface: where, find_by and the sanitisation helpers that distinguish parameterised from concatenated queries.
OpenSSL peer verification controls, relevant when assessing whether a server-side fetch validates the upstream it reaches.
Git attributes: export-ignore and pathspec handling, relevant to source-archive extraction paths that may preserve links.
OpenAPI 3.1: request bodies and content types, for reasoning about preflighted versus simple cross-origin requests.
CVSS v3.0 metric definitions: the Scope and Privileges-Required metrics that determine whether an authorization finding is scored as a lateral movement.
Android security tips: input-validation and untrusted-source guidance, plus the WebView trust boundary.
Vue security guide: framework auto-escaping, v-html, URL-injection via javascript:, and style-injection as clickjacking rather than script execution.
Community OAuth reference on PKCE grant usage; background for the code_challenge substitution bypass.
Ory Hydra OAuth2/OIDC server documentation: consent, redirect URI handling and client registration configuration.
Redis data types and command semantics, relevant where an application uses a non-SQL store and the injection class changes shape.
Kernel path-lookup documentation: component resolution, dot-dot handling and symbolic-link substitution semantics.
Landlock: filesystem-level confinement that makes a symlink escape unreachable rather than merely filtered.
